verification.scope: Only feedback.details.mechanismOrProperty and feedback.details.scenarioApplication changed for all 18 objects; no semantic acceptance.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A repeated operation ID is safe only when it still denotes the same command payload. The amount changed, so this is key reuse conflict, not a retry of the committed release.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The original release remains associated with its original amount; the altered request cannot silently reuse that identity.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: An idempotency key names a command payload; storing its fingerprint distinguishes a retry from key reuse.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: Operation op-428 remains tied to $80; the changed $95 request cannot silently claim that identity.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: Because validation stopped the command before persistence, there is no uncertain write to reconcile.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The corrected price can be evaluated independently because the earlier invalid request changed no stored state.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A validation failure before persistence has no stored state to reconcile.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The corrected price can be evaluated as a fresh command because the rejected input never mutated storage.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The expected revision is a write precondition; a stale edit must not replace a newer accepted geometry.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: An edit from revision 18 cannot overwrite geometry accepted as revision 19.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: An expected revision is a compare-before-write condition for concurrent edits.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The edit based on revision 18 cannot replace the geometry already accepted as revision 19.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The local notice and dispatch intent can be committed atomically, but provider delivery occurs later and may repeat.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The notice survives a worker crash with dispatch intent available for later delivery.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A transactional outbox stores local intent so dispatch can resume after a process interruption.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The notice remains committed with dispatch intent even if the worker stops before publishing.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: Each request can pass a read-time availability check before either write; the shared persistence boundary must decide which reservation is accepted.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: At most one overlapping reservation may become committed even when both requests observed availability.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: Concurrent requests must coordinate at the shared persistence boundary after their reads race.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: Only one overlapping meter reservation can commit even though both requests saw availability.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: Acknowledgement of queueing is not a terminal referral decision, so local status must not claim accepted or rejected yet.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The referral remains visibly pending until the specialist system reports a terminal outcome.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A queued acknowledgement describes request receipt, not completion of remote business processing.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The referral remains pending until the specialist system reports its terminal decision.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: Asset-level confirmation identifies which part of a permitted partial import remains unfinished.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: Confirmed assets remain complete while only unconfirmed asset work resumes.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: Per-item checkpoints distinguish confirmed effects from work that still needs resumption.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: Confirmed assets are skipped on resume while unconfirmed assets remain eligible for processing.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The confirmed seven units are known work; the timeout leaves only the five-unit vendor outcome unresolved.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The customer request and its confirmed quantity remain intact while the five-unit result is reconciled.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A partial outcome can be recorded without misclassifying an uncertain external remainder.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The original request keeps its seven confirmed units while the five-unit outcome is reconciled.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The stored Running state distinguishes this retry from both a completed result and a new experiment.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The caller receives the current run status without launching duplicate experiment work.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A durable operation state distinguishes in-progress work from completed and newly requested work.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: Run R-63 is reported as running after restart, without starting another execution.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The provider event ID identifies one delivery, while principal identity alone would collapse later legitimate grants.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: A repeated delivery is acknowledged without applying the grant transition again.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A delivery identifier scopes deduplication more narrowly than the recipient identity.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: A repeated provider event is acknowledged once while later grants for the same principal remain distinct.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A lease token distinguishes the current claim from the expired worker’s late completion.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The expired worker cannot complete the reminder now owned by the second lease.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A changing lease token fences completion from a worker whose claim has expired.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The first worker’s late result cannot complete the reminder under the second worker’s lease.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The two local records are one stated consistency boundary, so an interrupted half-write must not be visible.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: Neither the balance nor the allocation row can appear without the other.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A database transaction keeps related local writes within one commit boundary.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The balance and allocation row cannot become visible independently.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The system knows the persistence call never began; treating that as uncertain would invent a possible write.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The canceled attempt has no seal row because no write was attempted.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: Failure-stage knowledge determines whether a write outcome is uncertain or known absent.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The canceled seal attempt has no persisted record because execution stopped before the call.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The original inputs can change later, so the persisted revision pair is needed to reproduce this calculation.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: A later review can identify exactly which settlement and policy produced the amount.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: Persisting input revisions preserves the lineage needed to reproduce a historical calculation.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: Review can retrieve the settlement snapshot and policy version used for the original payout amount.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: Listing visibility is conditional on both submitted values passing together; separate commits expose an invalid intermediate state.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: Consumers see the new listing only after price and stock form one valid stored state.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A transaction can couple validation, storage, and visibility for values sharing one local consistency rule.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: A listing becomes visible only with the accepted price and stock combination.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The stable provider key identifies the same archive asset across the repeated batch.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: A repeated provider row updates metadata on the same archive asset.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A stable external key maps repeated deliveries to one persisted identity.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The second batch updates descriptive fields on the existing archive asset.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The provider reference supports status lookup, but the case gives no safe repeat-send guarantee while status is unknown.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The notice stays pending until the feed reports delivery status; no unsafely repeated send is inferred.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A status query can resolve uncertainty only through a capability the provider actually exposes.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The notice stays pending until the feed reports status for its request reference; resend safety is not assumed.

priorDetails.mechanismOrProperty: The first cancellation is committed; replaying the same command should resolve to its existing terminal outcome.
priorDetails.scenarioApplication: The reservation stays canceled, and the repeated command returns that committed outcome.

currentDetails.mechanismOrProperty: A committed terminal command can resolve a repeated request from its stored outcome.
currentDetails.scenarioApplication: The reservation stays canceled and the same cancellation command returns its original result.
